name: Jurinkika Freshness
author: jurinkika

sections.description:
Content ages quietly. A post that says “the best tools of 2023” or “currently the price is” is wrong a year later, and readers notice before you do. Jurinkika Freshness finds those places for you.

What it looks for

  • Earlier years next to a dating word: “in 2023”, “since 2019”, “for 2024”, “2022 guide”, “as of 2021”.
  • An earlier year anywhere in the title.
  • Phrases that date a text, in English and Dutch: “last year”, “this year”, “currently”, “at the moment”, “recently”, “coming soon”, “vorig jaar”, “momenteel”, “binnenkort” and more.
  • Your own phrases: an old product name, a price, an address you no longer use.
  • Content that nobody reviewed or changed for longer than a period you choose (12 months by default).

Where you see it

  • Tools > Freshness lists all content with what to check first, with every finding in its sentence.
  • A Freshness box in the editor shows the findings of the post you are working on. Tick “I have reviewed this text” to set the review date to today.
  • A Freshness column in the post and page lists.
  • A dashboard widget with the five posts to check first.

On the site (optional)

  • A “Last reviewed” line with the date under reviewed posts.
  • The review date for search engines, as schema.org lastReviewed.

Private by design

Everything runs on your own site. The plugin makes no outside requests, loads nothing from other servers, and stores its results in your own database.

Text is checked when you save it. For existing content, press “Scan all content” once on the overview; it works through your site in small batches.

Need more?

Jurinkika Content Health adds dead links with archived copies, broken images, removed videos, parked domains, a check that can stop publishing until it is fixed, and a weekly digest by mail. Jurinkika Freshness is complete on its own and stays free.
sections.installation:
1. Install the plugin through Plugins > Add New, or upload the folder to /wp-content/plugins/.
  2. Activate it.
  3. Go to Tools > Freshness and press Scan all content.
  4. Choose what to look for under Tools > Freshness > Settings.
sections.faq:
Does it change my content?

No. It only reads your content and shows what to check. You decide what to change.

Does it slow down my site?

No. Checks run in the admin, when you save a post or press the scan button. Visitors only get the optional “Last reviewed” line.

Which languages does it recognise?

The built-in phrases are English and Dutch. You can add phrases in any language under Settings, and developers can change the list with the jkfr_relative_phrases filter.

What happens when I delete the plugin?

The settings, the findings and the review dates are removed from the database.

short_description: Find posts that go out of date: earlier years, phrases like "last year" and "currently", and content nobody has reviewed for a long time.
